trips.title: Andorra High Route: Comapedrosa, Juclà and the Madriu Valley
trips.sub: Vall del Madriu-Perafita-Claror & Parc Natural Comunal de les Valls del Comapedrosa
trips.summary: Andorra is 468 km² and nearly all of it is above 1,000 m, which makes it the densest walking country in the Pyrenees. This week takes its two defining landscapes: the granite bowl beneath **Pic de Comapedrosa, 2,942 m**, the country's high point, and the Vall del Madriu-Perafita-Claror, a UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape covering nine per cent of the national territory with no road into it at all. Between them the route crosses the Sorteny and Juclà lake basins on the Coronallacs circuit. You sleep in a mixture of staffed refuges with cooked dinners and free unstaffed stone shelters. It suits confident hikers who like high, empty, lake-strewn granite country and do not need a village every night.

trips.title: Sutjeska and Zelengora: Maglić, Perućica and the Via Dinarica White Trail
trips.sub: Sutjeska National Park, Zelengora & the upper Drina, Republika Srpska
trips.summary: Sutjeska is Bosnia's oldest national park and the only place in Europe where you can walk from a Yugoslav-modernist war memorial into an untouched primeval forest and up the country's highest mountain in three days. **Maglić, 2,386 m**, is a proper limestone peak with chains on its upper gully; Perućica is 1,400 hectares of virgin beech and fir that you may only enter with a ranger; Zelengora behind it is a rolling green plateau strung with a dozen glacial lakes the locals call *gorske oči*, mountain eyes. It is empty, cheap, logistically rough and among the finest walking in south-east Europe. It suits self-sufficient hikers who are comfortable with cash economies, bad roads and unmarked ground.

trips.title: Mount Olympus Refuges: Petrostrouga, the Muses Plateau and Mytikas
trips.sub: Central Macedonia & Thessaly, Olympus National Park, Pieria
trips.summary: Olympus is far more mountain than its mythology suggests: a limestone massif rising from a beach to 2,918 m in 18 kilometres, with a summit that is a genuine scramble rather than a walk. This week climbs it the sensible way, up the forested Gortsia ridge to Petrostrouga, onto the Plateau of the Muses, over Mytikas and Skolio, and then a long descent through the Enipeas gorge to Litochoro and the sea. The refuges are cheap, sociable and Greek in character, meaning enormous dinners and no nonsense about check-in times. It suits fit hikers with scrambling experience; the summit ridge is the crux and not everyone should attempt it.

trips.title: Alta Via 1 in Seven Days: Braies to the Civetta Wall
trips.sub: Dolomiti Bellunesi & Ampezzane, Fanes-Sennes-Braies, Lagazuoi, Civetta
trips.summary: The Alta Via 1 is the Dolomites' introductory grand traverse and the one that actually delivers on the postcard: turquoise Braies, the high karst desert of Fanes and Sennes, the Great War tunnels bored through Lagazuoi, then a full day walking beneath the 1,200 m Civetta wall. Compressed into seven days it becomes serious walking, 5 to 8 hours daily, twelve passes, and no rest day, but it stays a hiking route, not a climbing one. You sleep in rifugi with duvets, three-course dinners and a wine list, which is why the beds vanish in February. It suits confident hill walkers who want altitude and scenery without needing rope work.

trips.title: Peaks of the Balkans: Rugova, Doberdol and the Three-Border Passes
trips.sub: Prokletije / Accursed Mountains, Rugova, Valbona, Theth & Plav
trips.summary: This is the wildest walking week in Europe that still has beds at the end of every day. The Prokletije are limestone in its most aggressive mood, 2,500 m walls, sinkhole basins, snow lying in shaded gullies in July, and the trail threads three countries with a shepherd economy still functioning above 1,700 m. You sleep in Rugova guesthouses, in tin-roofed katun dormitories at Doberdol where the water comes from a pipe in a hillside, and in Theth and Valbona stone houses where dinner is whatever the family cooked. It suits hikers who want genuine remoteness and can tolerate paperwork, rough transfers and inconsistent waymarking. It is emphatically not a Dolomites-style hut circuit: bring your own margin.

trips.title: Triglav Hut-to-Hut: Vrata, Kredarica and the Seven Lakes
trips.sub: Julian Alps & Triglav National Park, Vrata, Kredarica, Triglavska jezera, Bohinj
trips.summary: Triglav is a national obsession compressed into one mountain, and this week climbs it the honest way, up the Vrata valley from 1,015 m, over the summit at 2,864 m, then away from the crowds south across the Hribarice plateau into the Valley of the Seven Lakes and down to Bohinj. Day two is the hardest day's walking in Slovenia outside a rope; day three is a cabled ridge with 800 m of air on the left. After that the week softens into high karst, larch, glacial tarns and a lake swim. It suits fit hikers who are comfortable with exposure and clipped into a self-belay kit, not first-time mountain walkers.

trips.title: Ordesa y Monte Perdido: Góriz, the Fajas and the GR-11
trips.sub: Aragonese Pyrenees, Ordesa y Monte Perdido National Park, Sobrarbe
trips.summary: Ordesa is the Pyrenees at their most architectural: a 15 km glacial trench with 900 m walls, terraced by *fajas*, horizontal ledges a metre wide that let you walk across the cliff face, and closed at its head by the Cola de Caballo. Above it sits Monte Perdido, 3,355 m, the highest limestone mountain in Europe, and around it three more canyons of the same family: Añisclo, Escuaín and Pineta. This week uses Refugio de Góriz as a two-night base for the summit, then crosses out through Añisclo to Pineta and returns over the north-side fajas. It suits strong hill walkers who can handle a snow slope with crampons and are not troubled by exposure on a ledge.
